STEP 1 - Scene: A airline-style tray meal: a fruit cup (cut melon, apple, strawberries, orange pieces) in a small white bowl, a baked cannelloni-style pasta roll (two rolled pasta tubes with cheese/meat filling and browned top) on a white plate, plus a glass of orange juice and a glass of water.

STEP 2 - Vessel: Main plate is a white paper plate, about 20 cm diameter. Area = 3.14 x 10^2 = 314 cm². The fruit bowl is about 15 cm diameter (area ~177 cm²) and sits separately; I count it as part of this meal.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) pasta rolls with cheese/meat filling and tomato-based sauce, (b) mixed fruit pieces (melon, apple, strawberry, orange), (c) orange juice (liquid, separate glass), (d) water (separate glass, no energy).

STEP 4 - Area (of the 314 cm² plate): pasta rolls cover ~40% of the plate area (about 125 cm²). Fruit bowl covers ~177 cm² of its own vessel; treated as its own vessel, so the fruit is ~100% of its bowl.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Pasta rolls: 125 cm² x 3.5 cm (two stacked rolls, outer envelope) = 438 ml.
- Fruit: bowl interior ~177 cm² x 3 cm (heaped pieces) = 530 ml.
- Orange juice: ~200 ml glass, roughly 150 ml served.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Pasta rolls: 438 ml x 0.9 = 394 g. (Pasta rolls are lighter and hollow-ish, so I keep the 0.9 density as the only reduction; this gives roughly 390 g.)
- Fruit: 530 ml x 0.6 = 318 g.
- Orange juice: 150 g.
- Water: 200 g (0 kcal).

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Baked pasta roll with cheese/meat filling: ~170 kcal/100 g → 394 g x 1.7 = 670 kcal.
- Mixed fruit: ~50 kcal/100 g → 318 g x 0.5 = 159 kcal.
- Orange juice: ~45 kcal/100 g → 150 g x 0.45 = 68 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A large baked pasta roll portion with two tubes, plus a generous fruit cup and juice, totalling roughly 860 g and about 900 kcal, is plausible for an airline main-plus-fruit meal. The pasta estimate is the most uncertain part, since the rolls may be partly air-filled; I stayed with the stated density as the only reduction.

Total food (excluding water): about 862 g, about 897 kcal.
